findings.title: Flask debug mode enables Werkzeug debugger
findings.evidence: app.run(debug=True); startup log shows 'Debugger is active! Debugger PIN: 753-725-197' and /console returns HTTP 200.
findings.remediation: Never enable debug via the run path: gate it on an env var (app.run(debug=os.environ.get('FLASK_DEBUG') == '1')) and deploy behind a real WSGI server (gunicorn/waitress) in production.

findings.title: No auth on state-mutating POST /update_player
findings.evidence: curl -X POST /update_player -d '{"x":1,"y":2,"id":999}' -> 200 {"status":"ok"} with no credential required; no auth check exists anywhere in the app.
findings.remediation: Add an auth middleware (Flask before_request checking Bearer token or flask-login session) and object-level authorization binding player ids to the caller; document the unauthenticated posture if this stays a demo.

findings.title: No API spec; endpoints are stubs returning {"status":"ok"}
findings.evidence: No OpenAPI/GraphQL/proto file in repo; both routes return hardcoded {'status':'ok'} regardless of input; git log -- app.py shows 2 commits and no versioning.
findings.remediation: Write a minimal OpenAPI 3.x spec (or generate via flask-smorest/apispec) describing both routes and their schemas; version under /api/v1/ if the API will evolve.

findings.title: No input validation on /update_player body
findings.evidence: request.get_json() result is unused; arbitrary JSON ({"x":1,"y":2,"id":999}) returns 200. Verified with curl.
findings.remediation: Validate the body with a pydantic model or voluptuous/flask-expect schema (typed x/y coordinates, bounded values) returning 422 with field errors on mismatch.

findings.title: No request size limit
findings.evidence: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH unset; a ~5MB JSON body was accepted and parsed (400 only due to malformed JSON, not size).
findings.remediation: Set app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'] (e.g. 16-64KB) so oversized bodies get an automatic 413.

findings.title: Error responses are Werkzeug HTML, not JSON; inconsistent envelope
findings.evidence: Malformed JSON -> 400 text/html 'Failed to decode JSON object: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'; unknown route -> 404 text/html. Success is application/json. No request/correlation ids.
findings.remediation: Register JSON error handlers returning an RFC 9457 application/problem+json envelope (type, title, status, detail, instance) for 4xx/5xx, plus an X-Request-ID header echoed to logs.

findings.title: No application logging or health/readiness endpoint
findings.evidence: Zero logging calls beyond Werkzeug access log; no /healthz, metrics, or tracing hooks; 5xx not alertable.
findings.remediation: Use Python logging with python-json-logger for structured logs, add a /healthz route, and propagate request ids.

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.evidence: Response headers contain only Server/Date/Content-Type/Content-Length - no CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, or Referrer-Policy (verified via curl -si /).
findings.remediation: Add flask-talisman (or an after_request hook) with a baseline header set; configure CSP to match the static JS bundle.

findings.title: npm dependencies: 1 critical + 37 high vulnerabilities, fix available
findings.evidence: npm audit --audit-level=high -> 44 vulnerabilities (2 low, 4 moderate, 37 high, 1 critical), 'fix available via npm audit fix'; includes ws and @babel/plugin-transform-modules-systemjs arbitrary-code CVE. pip-audit on requirements.txt is clean.
findings.remediation: Run npm audit fix (and npm audit fix --force for the rest) and add npm audit --audit-level=high as a CI gate.

findings.title: No rate limiting on POST endpoint
findings.evidence: No throttling on /update_player; unbounded POST rate accepted in testing.
findings.remediation: Add flask-limiter with a per-IP limit (e.g. 60/min) on mutating routes.

findings.title: No CI, contract tests, changelog, or deprecation policy
findings.evidence: No .github/workflows, no spec linting, no changelog, no documented deploy/rollback path.
findings.remediation: Add a minimal GitHub Actions workflow running npm test, pip-audit/npm audit, and spectral lint once a spec exists.

positives: JSON routes consistently return application/json for success responses.
Correct method enforcement: GET /update_player returns 405 with Allow: POST, OPTIONS.
.gitignore covers venv/, .env*, node_modules/, coverage and build output - no secrets or environments committed.
No secrets, keys, or hardcoded credentials anywhere in code or config.
Python dependencies (Flask>=3.0.0, numpy>=1.26.0) are current and clean under pip-audit.
Real Jest test suite exists for static JS (npm test; 22/23 pass, one known pre-existing failure in test expectations).
Dev server binds localhost only by default - debug-mode exposure is not on all interfaces.
needs_confirmation: Whether the app is ever deployed anywhere other than local dev - if so, WSD-B-01 (debug mode) and WSD-B-02 (no auth) escalate to critical.
Effective rate-limiting need once /update_player actually mutates state (currently a stub).
CORS policy intent - no Access-Control-* headers are sent (restrictive default fits same-origin use but is undocumented).
